clue.text: Harangue family after help is withdrawn

indicators.note: after places the word for family behind the turned word for help
withdrawn is read as drawn back, so the word for help runs right to left

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a family group or clan

explanation.surface: A ranting speech from a family whose assistance has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like it describes the help being taken away, but it signals the turnaround; 'after' sets the family word behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, which is what a harangue is.

clue.text: Mirror — I finish the game holding it

indicators.note: holding means the word for ending a chess game contains it

parts.note: mate finishes a game of chess

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to end the match while hanging on to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish the game' points to chess, where checkmate ends play; 'holding' wraps that word round 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy them exactly.

clue.text: During a coup, many hide

indicators.note: during means the letter for many sits inside the word for a coup

parts.note: a takeover is a seizure of power, a coup
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: In the middle of a military coup, lots of people go into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To take cover is to shelter or conceal oneself.

clue.text: Pacific isle — isle overrun by French, excluding outsiders

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for isle again

indicators.note: overrun by means the second isle letter is surrounded by the letters taken from French
excluding outsiders removes the first and last letters of the word French

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for isle again

explanation.surface: An island in the Pacific invaded by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding outsiders' cuts FRENCH to RENC, and 'overrun by' puts the second I inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic means peaceable or conciliatory, an older sense of pacific.

clue.text: Pine used in the construction of a rotten tea-house

indicators.note: the letters of a rotten tea-house are the building material, rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Pine wood was used to build a dilapidated tea-house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in the construction of' rearranges A ROTTEN TEA-HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long hopelessly, which is grieving and yearning to the point of torment.

clue.text: Collected cape in cloth

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for cape inside the word for cloth

parts.note: plaid is a tartan woollen cloth
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Someone composed despite wearing a cape made of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Collected in the sense of calm and composed is a synonym.

clue.text: Kings and queens and noble tucked into food

indicators.note: tucked into means the nobleman goes inside the word for food

parts.note: pies are food
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Royalty and an aristocrat sitting down to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers who wear clothes covered in pearl buttons for charity events.
explanation.definitionFit: London's pearly kings and queens are known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Prudence, an amusing person

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a comic or entertaining character

explanation.surface: A girl called Prudence described as great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means wariness and also, informally, a droll character.

clue.text: Wife comes before a popsy, a play thing

indicators.note: comes before places the word for wife ahead of the word for popsy

parts.note: in Cockney, my old Dutch means my wife
doll and popsy are both dated slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: A man's wife arrives ahead of his girlfriend, which is all a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' as wife is Cockney, from 'duchess'. A Dutch doll is a jointed wooden doll.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch doll is a wooden toy, something to play with.

clue.text: Preserve = jam

definitions.meaning: a vinegar or brine conserve of vegetables

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style equation saying that preserve and jam are the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a vegetable conserve and a fix or awkward situation share this word.

clue.text: Correction thus applied excessively

definitions.meaning: a correction is applied to an error, i.e. to a mistake
overdoing a virtue, as in generous beyond reason

explanation.surface: A note about a correction being laid on too heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both where a correction goes (onto a mistake) and an idiom for overdoing something.

clue.text: Permit contains some changes

indicators.note: some changes made to the word contains rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: A licence that includes a number of amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some changes' rearranges the letters of CONTAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or allow it.

clue.text: Liberal Whip to retain missile

indicators.note: to retain means the word for whip holds the missile within it

parts.note: to lash is to whip
the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI

explanation.surface: A Liberal party whip trying to keep hold of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, so 'missile' gives VI. 'Liberal Whip' looks like a party official, but Liberal is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and liberal both mean generous or given freely.

clue.text: Minister to open the rally perhaps

definitions.meaning: to attend to or wait on someone
in tennis the first stroke of a rally is the delivery

explanation.surface: A government minister launching a political rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to someone's needs and to put the ball in play in tennis share the word.

clue.text: A thrusting fellow, ending as a lyric-writer

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the word as

parts.note: a wordsman is a skilled user of words, such as a writer of lyrics

explanation.surface: An ambitious man who ends up writing song lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer lunges and thrusts with a blade, so he is a thrusting fellow.

clue.text: "No repeats to be broadcast" in Zamenhof's words

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of no repeats are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's promise of no reruns, quoted from Zamenhof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be broadcast' rearranges the letters of NO REPEATS. L. L. Zamenhof invented the international language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwik Zamenhof created this constructed language, so its vocabulary is his words.

clue.text: A curtain smothers husband — it falls with crushing effect

indicators.note: smothers means the word for curtain covers the abbreviation for husband

parts.note: a valance is a short curtain or drape

explanation.surface: A drape falls on a husband and crushes him.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain buries whatever is below.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's head showing distress

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its first letter

parts.note: weeping means crying, showing distress

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's headteacher in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive school' looks like the British state school; Comprehensive alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging or all-embracing.

clue.text: Charles II gave promise in almost cowardly about-turn

indicators.note: an about-turn faces the whole assembly the other way, so it is read backwards
in puts the word for promise inside the shortened word for cowardly
almost means the word for cowardly loses its final letter

parts.note: yellow means cowardly
to give one's word is to promise

explanation.surface: A king made a pledge during a nearly spineless climbdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the colour word, 'in' and 'about-turn' then work on the whole, giving YELWORDLO turned round. Old Rowley was Charles II's nickname, after his racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Rowley was the nickname of the English king, taken from a favourite stallion.

clue.text: Precipitate cooking of topside

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of topside are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: Cooking a joint of beef in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking of' rearranges TOPSIDE, a British cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: To precipitate is to make a solid settle out of a liquid, laying down sediment.

clue.text: Provided money and aid to the chairman

parts.note: gave means provided
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone supplied cash and help to the company chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman bangs this mallet to keep order, so it is a tool that helps him.

clue.text: Make river attractive

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
cute means attractive

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a river pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out or produce a work is a synonym of make.

clue.text: It's necessary to assemble many a sign

indicators.note: the letters needed are found by joining parts of the words assemble many

explanation.surface: Building a sign takes plenty of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or badge, a kind of sign.

clue.text: Herbert in the finish rejected girl

indicators.note: in puts Herbert's initials inside the turned word for finish
rejected is read as thrown back, so the word for finish runs backwards

parts.note: end means finish
the humorist A. P. Herbert signed his work with his initials

explanation.surface: Herbert, at the end, turned down a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the word for finish round to DNE before 'in' acts. A. P. Herbert was an English humorist and MP who signed himself A.P.H.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a female first name, an example of a girl.

clue.text: Went berserk and stormed about current measure

indicators.note: about means the word for stormed goes round the unit of current

parts.note: raged means stormed
the amp measures electric current

explanation.surface: Someone flew into a fury over an electrical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about wildly, which is going berserk.

clue.text: Fly medical men to the capital

parts.note: MOs are medical officers
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Instructions to fly doctors out to a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This biting insect is a kind of two-winged fly.

clue.text: My clue can be solved in a lecture-hall

indicators.note: solved here means worked out, so the letters of my clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter boasting that their clue can be cracked during a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be solved' rearranges the letters of MY CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a hall for public lectures, named after Aristotle's school.

clue.text: Seeing out the' first part of the, game

parts.note: not in means out

indicators.note: the first part of the word game is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Watching someone sit out the opening stage of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means observing or perceiving, a synonym of seeing.

clue.text: Vale to Communist made more acceptable

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe is a valley in Greece
a red is a Communist

explanation.surface: A valley bequeathed to a Communist, now more palatable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vale of Tempe is a valley in Thessaly, Greece, praised by classical poets.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or moderate it, making it easier to accept.
